utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I thought I'd take this opportunity before the witness is called to deal with some matters. First, the remaining number of witnesses and hours for the Defence case, I am to say that the Chamber will issue an order shortly indicating the number of hours left in the Defence case. The Defence will be aware that some hours have already been lost for reasons which are very well known to it. The next matter relates to the question of experts. Mr. Ivetic, we have been told that you intend to call six experts, but we have received neither reports nor a full statement, and as you're aware, the other party must have 30 days in which to respond. The Chamber will issue an order shortly setting time limits in relation to this matter. Again, Mr. Ivetic, you have a request for a video-link. You're seeking to have these witnesses video-linked next week, I believe, but as you would know, two weeks' notice is required for the Registry to make these arrangements. The Chamber will immediately order that you file medical certificates supporting the submissions made in annex B to the motion filed on Friday, the 16th of January, and these must -- the certificates must be filed by Friday the 16th, and I want to stress that this is to be done by 4 p.m. The next matter relates to -- I believe we have to go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for the witness, Your Honour, if I could just inquire as to the time remaining for Mr. Groome in cross-examination of the sitting witness given the Court's ruling as to MLD15. I need to make sure the victims and witnesses has sufficient time to bring the next witness in after the completion of the direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just before the bring the witness, let me inquire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecutor took an hour and 23 minutes. The Defence has so far used ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. It's the other way around. The Defence took an hour and 23 minutes, and the Prosecutor has so far used an hour and 6 minutes. In the circumstances, Mr. Groome, I'll give you another 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please call the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, such a long time has elapsed. I think we'll have the witness make the declaration again. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'd like to resume my questions to you on the topic of evidence that you gave last time with respect to your brother and your uncle being with Milan Lukic on the 27th and 28th of June. My first question to you is, is your uncle with them at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could perhaps have a transcript reference. I think Mr. Groome has misspoken as to the prior evidence, but I must have got some other transcript reference, I thought it was -- I don't want to influence the testimony, but I think it's another individual and the brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you, you've given evidence that Milan Lukic was with your father and your brother on St. Vitus day in 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was your uncle with them at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. My father told me that they were at Milan Lukic's place, the father and the brother. I don't know about my uncle, whether he was there, too, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, if I recall your testimony correctly, it's that after the female members of your family fled (redacted), your father and your brother remained behind to take care of the livestock on the family farm in (redacted). Have I remembered your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, over the break I've had an opportunity to look at your brother's statement, and I must put to you that it contradicts you in several important regards, and the first one that I -- the first way that it contradicts you is that according to your brother, your father was living in the town -- in the area of Visegrad known as (redacted), which is just south of the town. Are you sure it's your -- or do you maintain it's your evidence that your father was living in the area of (redacted) during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father was living in (redacted) throughout, and he did not move at any point. It was my brother who owned a house in (redacted), not this brother that we're talking about but the other, late brother of mine, who was killed at one point, owned a house in (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, let me read from paragraph 2 of your brother's statement what he says about where your father was to see if it refreshes your recollection about what that brother told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does that cause you to change your evidence about where your father was in the spring of 1992 and whether or not he was -- remained in (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the cause for speculation if they're presenting the statement of a person who's not in this courtroom. This is the type of thing that this honorable Trial Chamber has denied the Defence the opportunity to do with Prosecution witnesses time and again, and Mr. Groome has objected time and again, and he's taking this statement, this particular section of the statement that does not comport to the question he'd asked previously, and he's speculating as to what this individual meant when he made this statement. So I would object that it's an out-of-court declaration of a person who's not present, and for the law of the case that we've developed in this case, it should not be used to present to this witness. There are countless Prosecution witnesses that we tried to present statements by family members on pertinent issues, and we were denied that opportunity. So I think that quality of arms and fairness dictate that Mr. Groome --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. We prohibited questions of that nature in response to submissions from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be heard, there's a very important difference here, and the difference is that this woman has testified that the man who made this statement told her that the father lived in (redacted). I'm putting to her his statement that he says the father was not living in (redact). He was living in (redact), so it's very different from a situation where I'm putting something that's completely unrelated. She's given evidence about what the declarant of this statement has said to her, and when we look at the statement of this man, it's something completely different. It's a very different situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'll be brief, but in that case I'd ask to call back all the Prosecution witnesses. I remember one in particular. I think it was K-64 who said her husband said that Milan Lukic took him away. We tried to present the sworn statement of the Prosecutor of the husband that said that it was not Milan Lukic, and we were denied that opportunity, so again I believe it's the exact same situation, and Mr. Groome is trying to draw straws where there aren't any. It's the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I also note I'm not seeking to introduce this statement as Defence counsel sought to introduce theirs. I'm simply putting what the brother has said about it, just to see if it causes her to alter her testimony here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the Chamber considers that it is essentially the same -- the same kind of objection that was raised in the Prosecution's case. We will not allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Am I permitted to ask if it refreshes her recollection as to what her brother may have said to her, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that that will have the same effect, so move on to another area, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, is it not a fact that your father during this period of time, the time that you say that he was still in (redacted), was not in (redacted) at all but was living in the town of Visegrad? Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know my father told me that he was living in (redacted), and he was living in (redacted). He was living in (redacted). Now, he probably was in a position to travel to (redacted), as well, because his son's house was over there, so he may have spent some time in (redacted), but he was never actually living there in terms of being resident there, not as far as I know, but I wasn't at home all the time so maybe at some point in time he 17 was spending time in (redacted). And I certainly can't be expected to comment on my brother's statement because they were together. I know my father told me that they were together. Did he go to (redacted) or not at the time is not something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, when did your father die?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three years ago. Three or four years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you told us in response to a question from Mr. Ivetic that after your husband died, you moved back from Montenegro, and you moved to Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And your husband died in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to read to you a portion of a question Mr. Ivetic posed to you and your answer and then ask you a question about it, and this is -- I'm quoting from transcript 3965. "Now, madam, madam, you had started testifying about when you had moved to Zenica and had met up with your family, that is to say your brother -- pardon me, your father, and they told you everything. Could you please try to complete your answer to my question which originally was that, Did you ever have an opportunity to confirm with your family members whether Milan gave this gift packet to them as you had requested him to do? "A: Yes, my father confirmed that and so did my brother." My question to you is that you spoke with your father and your brother about these events after you returned to Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to my relatives even before I came to visit. We'd spoken about that. I asked them about that because I'd been there once with my husband who died in Bosnia after the war. And also after this, when I came back, I spoke about the war to them. They told me about their experience, how they got through the whole thing, and told me about all of this because I wasn't in Bosnia myself at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was it that your father or your brother first confirmed to you this account that you've relayed about St. Vitus Day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother confirmed this when I came to visit with my husband. I left with my husband for the barracks and I brought him back home so that we could see him and speak to him, and we talked about his experience during the war, and he told me that he had received a gift from Milan Lukic, which is something that I had sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Miss, I understand. I'm just asking you when, what year, and if you're able, what month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been in 2000. It was a year before my husband died that I traveled to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So at the very earliest, five years after the war is the first time that your brother and your father confirmed to you this event that you've described for us. It's five years, correct, after the war ended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your answer has not been recorded for the record. Can I ask you maybe just to speak a little bit closer to the mike?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And eight years after the event itself, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long after the event, but I know that it was then that they told me this. They hadn't really had an opportunity previously, and I didn't know their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you just explain that, why you say that "they hadn't really had an opportunity previously ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There had never been an opportunity previously. I didn't go there. I didn't know their whereabouts. I didn't speak to them, and I didn't go to Bosnia myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've been put forward as a character witness, as well, and I want to be clear, you were not an eye-witness to any of the events that occurred in Visegrad in the spring of 1992. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And your evidence relating to Milan Lukic's character is based on what you have testified about here, that he was a good neighbor to your family growing up and that he helped your brother and father in 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you left Visegrad in 1990 and did not see Milan Lukic until 1992. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And between 1992 and the time you saw him in the courtroom here in December, you had not had any interaction with him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you do know that Milan Lukic left Visegrad when he completed his training at secondary school; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So most of your knowledge of Milan Lukic related to his character is based upon your experience of him prior to the time he left secondary school in Visegrad ; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct. I did see him back in 1990 as well. We had a talk, and I'd never heard anyone in Visegrad municipality or in my village say anything other than the impression that I had of his character, that is, before the war. Now, as to now, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But based on your own personal experience of him, most of that relates to the time when he was a boy. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't exactly a boy. I'm talking about 1990. The war began in 1992. Even during the war, if you look at it that way, he was still a boy. He might have been, what, 23 to 25 years of age or thereabouts, so -- well, a boy, not a completely mature man, you might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But my point is when you use words like gracious, extremely humane, nice, noble, positive character, as far as you've based that on your own personal experience of him, that really relates to the time when you were living in (redacted) and he was a neighbor of yours and you had regular interaction with him. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have not spoken directly to any survivors of some of the crimes that occurred in Visegrad and may say something different about Milan Lukic, have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never had an opportunity to talk to the many such people. The one opportunity that I did have was when I saw something on TV. It was SENSE, the agency, broadcasting trials from the Tribunal, but all the things that I keep hearing indicate that an entirely different person is being described here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to last December. When you testified about trying to contact Milan Lukic to find out about your family, did you make any efforts with other people prior to trying to contact Milan Lukic? Were there other people you sought this information from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who were they, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that I once got in touch with Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe when that was and summarise the conversation you had with Mr. Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime before I contacted Milan. He said he knew nothing about my family. He was sorry. He said that he hadn't really gone to Visegrad much and that he was sorry not to be able to share more than that with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Sreten Lukic the only other person that you attempt to contact to get information about your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to contact his sister, Miljana Lukic. I forget what her married name is. She's a cousin, and she was living in Uzice, and I called her to see if she knew anything about my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, with your evidence with respect to contacting Milan Lukic, it's your evidence that after several years after both you and Milan Lukic have moved away from Visegrad that you call his sister on a particular day, and it just so happens that Milan Lukic is in the vicinity of his sister, and he calls you back that very same day. That's your evidence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was the first time you had contact with any member of the Milan Lukic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll object to the relevance, Your Honour. How is that relevant to the testimony of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, every Prosecution witness nearly has been asked about contacts with Prosecution lawyers and investigators. I mean, certainly the number of times that she has had conversations about this case with members of the Defence team is something relevant and subject to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, who was the first person that you had contact with with respect to this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first and last persons were the lawyers, the members of the team that I described, the people who signed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And those are the people that came to your home on the 22nd of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was when they took my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you had no contact with any other members of the team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the names of those two people were Mr. Rasic and Mr. Lakcevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the family name of the other man was. I know his name was Vladimir, but that's all I can remember. I can't remember the other man's name. There is a signature on my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If someone had a good friend that was named Vladimir, what would be the familiar form of Vladimir that one would use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. I don't know what that person would be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would the familiar form of Vladimir not be Vlado?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that it would be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, during the course of your direct testimony, you refer to one of the people that came to see you in your house twice as Vlado. At Transcript 3979, you said: "Vlado was in a pair of shorts." "Vlado was wearing jeans." Are you sure you only met with Mr. Rasic, or Vladimir, the person you know as Vladimir, on this occasion, only once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was when he took my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, on the 18th of December, you testified how Milan Lukic helped your brother and father escape (redacted) by escorting them down to the Drina River where relatives of yours from the other side of the Drina crossed over in a boat and took them across. When you testified to this, you never mentioned your uncle. My question to you is, was your uncle 19 with them at the time that he went down to the Drina and escaped (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's actually I think a translation issue. The term "boat" translates into a -- it's a little bit difficult to discuss in English. In B/C/S, it translates into "brodom" [phoen], which is a large ship, whereas the witness I believe in her testimony in the transcript talked about a "camac", which is a smaller type of vessel, so just putting that out there, that the word that's being used in the English has alternate meanings in B/C/S that are not quite comporting to the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a boat, and my uncle -- I don't know whether anybody else was with them. What I do know is that there were my brother and my father there with them. Could you repeat your question maybe? I did not understand it quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question to you is, at the time when Milan Lukic escorts your father and your brother to the Drina and they escape safely, is your uncle with them? Does he escape at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he wasn't. They didn't tell me that he was. It's possible that he was there, but they didn't mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know how your uncle would have escaped if he was not with them at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My uncle and all my family and relatives had departed for Zepa previously. Nobody was chasing them. They just left that place. When the shooting started, when the war started, they moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence today that your uncle left with the female members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they left home, all of them, the men would on occasion return as needed to their homes to collect items, food, clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your evidence now that your father and brother had left Visegrad and had been returning to (redacted) periodically? Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that when it concerns my father and brother, but I'm talking about my uncle and the other members of the family, they would come back on occasion. They had stowed away food, flour. They would take out such items from the house to the forest and then would come back to collect them. This is what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then later in your testimony on the 18th of December, you testify that after Milan Lukic helped your father and brother escape, they returned to get the three family cows, and they brought them across the Drina on a boat. Do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, and this is how it unfolded. We had many heads of cattle, and they managed to transfer all of their cattle across the Drina River to the other bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that Milan Lukic helps your father and brother escape with their lives from (redacted), and yet they return, collect their cattle, and walk them down what I believe you said was about a half-hour walk to the banks of the Drina and then bring them across the Drina on a boat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They drove their cattle to the river, and then later on my relatives, my cousins, helped them to transfer the cattle across the river to the other bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I want to change topics, and I want to put some of your evidence to you from the 18th of December. At transcript page 3988, you were asked the following question by Mr. Ivetic: "Madam Witness, do you have any knowledge or information as to any pressure, threats or intimidation experienced by your brother, MLD2, who you know as," and I won't say the name," relating to his decision to become a witness to the Defence of Milan Lukic." And you answered: "Yes, I do have knowledge of that, and I was told that we should not contact him over the phone at all because he's being harassed all the time. He's receiving phone calls, and this is 100 per cent the work of Vilic." My first question to you based on this excerpt from your testimony, is how did you know this was happening to your brother if you had not spoken to him for a year before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew if I'm not talking to my brother, other members of the family talked to him, and this is how I came to know about that from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you say: "I was told that I should not contact him." Who told you that you should not contact your brother, MLD2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of those who knew that he had received threats told me -- I heard from other members of the family that he had received threats and that it would not be advisable for me to contact him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to put some of the assertions that Mr. Hamdija Vilic has testified to. He says that while he was waiting for the lawyers to appear, you and your husband told him that he would be provided with everything that he needed in life. Do you admit that you said this to him, or do you deny that you said this to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I surely did not say this to him because I couldn't provide such guarantees. I could not do so, and I saw no reason for me to tell him anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He further testified that while waiting, that you told him that you had taken 5.000 Euros to MLD2 which came from Milan Lukic as payment for him giving false testimony. Do you admit this, or do you deny this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He also says that when he was in your house, you received several calls. Do you recall receiving telephone calls while he was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. Nobody phoned me. The telephone was in the room where the Defence team members were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He stated that he believed the phone calls were from Milan Lukic. Did you speak with Milan Lukic any time on the day of the 22nd of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this was the 22nd of June or some other date because on the 22nd of June -- well, I don't know, but my statement was not given and signed on the 22nd but on the 23rd, but I couldn't be sure, and I wouldn't state it as a fact before checking, but I don't believe that it was on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the day Hamdija Vilic was in your home, did Milan Lukic call you and have a conversation with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, he did not call on that day. Defence team members had called me and asked whether he was there, the Defence lawyers, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Defence lawyers called you and asked you who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked whether Hamdija had arrived, Hamdija Vilic, because I had told them that he would be coming and that it was arranged for him to come to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask that we go briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, can you tell us without mentioning their name, just tell us their relationship to you, who in your family told you that you should not call MLD2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my foster mother told me that she didn't want this to be in the public domain, that she had heard that threats were issued against him, and that still threats are being issued against him and her, and that Hamdija's brother is still maintaining that I had sued Vilic and that he wrote -- read on the internet that I sued Hamdija.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to a different topic. At transcript 3974 on the 18th of December, Mr. Ivetic asked you: "And did in fact Mr. Hamdija Vilic on that occasion volunteer to be a witness for the Defence of Milan Lukic and meet with these members of the Defence team?" And you answered: "Yes. He asked to appear as a witness, but he didn't want to meet with them in Sarajevo but to meet with them at my place, and I accepted, although he was not a very close relative, and I didn't really feel like receiving anyone in my house." So my question to you is, is it Hamdija Vilic who contacted you and first raised the possibility of him testifying for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. If I can just ask for the transcript reference to be checked. I believe that she had said he was a close relative -- sorry, I believe that the negative, at line 25, 27 is out of place, but ... I have the uncorrected transcript in front of me, so I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying the transcript actually says that he was a close relative? Is that your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's my notes. I cannot check in the transcript that I have in front of me because I don't have the page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's on line number, Your Honour, I'm checking my copy, and it's that, but Mr. Ivetic can check the LiveNote for himself. And the transcript reference is 3974.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It says exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, what I'm asking you is it Hamdija Vilic that first contacted you and first raised the possibility of being a witness for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever -- is it not true that you were the one who asked him whether he would be a witness for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked him whether he want to be a witness, but he asked me, when phoning me to make sure that it took place at my place and no place else. He phoned me on the eve of that day and in the morning on that day that he would be leaving his house and whether he could come to my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So if I understand your last answer, you asked him if he wanted to be a witness for Milan Lukic; then he asked you, could he meet them at your house. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So Mr. Vilic is correct when he says that it is you that raised the prospect of him testifying in the Milan Lukic case. He's not wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Defence team asked me to give them his telephone number and asked me whether he would be testifying, and I told them I would be calling him, and he agreed but provided that this took place at my place. He didn't want to meet them in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, just today, a few moments ago you've told us that the only contact you had with the Defence was on the day that they came to your house. When did they call you and who called and you asked you to make contact with Hamdija Vilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same members of the Defence team, they called me earlier that they would be coming to my place and asked me to ask Hamdija whether he would be a witness. They had planned for me to go to Sarajevo to meet them there and not to come to my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you receive that phone call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days before they arrived, maybe two days, before they arrived to take my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who called you? Mr. Rasic, Vladimir, or Mr. Lakcevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vladimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any other phone calls or phone contact with Vladimir that perhaps you forgot to tell us about that you now remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll object to the characterization of this question. He's now attempting to badger the witness. His prior question to the witness was had she met with other members of the Defence team, I believe, is my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see any objection to the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, have you had any other contact by whatever means with other members of the Defence team that perhaps you recall now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've testified about Hamdija Vilic making a demand for 100.000 Euros of the two men that came to your home. Did that happen shortly after he began his discussion with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened quickly. First, I gave my statement; then he entered the room, but before the Defence team came, he told me over a cup of coffee that he would be seeking 100.000 Euro. I told him, who would give you 100.000 Euro? Are you crazy? And he said, well, whether they want or they don't want to give me the money, who fucks them? And that is literally what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that he made that demand of them as soon as he began to speak with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because they finished the conversation immediately, maybe five minutes, even less, spent together. As soon as he entered the room, he said that he demanded money, and then they gave up the idea of meeting with him. They said, well, we don't want to have dealings with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So they never really had any discussion with him about what evidence he might give, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, he agreed to give a statement and had promised to give a statement, but he demanded 100.000 Euro. I don't know whether he did actually give the statement, but as soon as they were asked for 100.000 Euro, they left, and they said, There's no point in having any business with him. I asked them whether they wanted my telephone number, and they said, No, we have no intention of calling you, we don't need your number, we have no intention of paying anybody 100.000 Euro, we don't want to give 1 Euro to anybody, let alone 100.000 Euro.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At any time in your house did you observe Hamdija Vilic give a statement to the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he spoke with them. I don't know whether they wrote down anything that he said. I did not want to eavesdrop on their conversation. We played some music, and I left that room for that purpose. I wasn't in that room when he was giving his statement, and he wasn't in the room when I was giving my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But what you said is that his interaction with him was less than five minutes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thereabouts. I did not really measure how long they stayed together, but he did not stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The difficulty, MLD10, that I'm facing is that if Hamdija Vilic is lying, and in fact this occurred the way you say it did, that he was in there for a very short period of time, he makes his demand for money, they end the conversation, if it happened that way, how is it that Hamdija Vilic knows the details of the alibi defence that's been put forward by Milan Lukic? It happened in Kopito, the date, how many people were killed. It's not possible for him to have known that, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I anticipate Mr. Ivetic is going to say that she can't explain how he would know that or not know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified that Hamdija Vilic's family burnt to death in the family home in Prelovo. Do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did make that statement. I heard about that when I returned from Montenegro to Bosnia, that they would talk about Hamdija's house and about his family being burned down at Prelovo. I did not know about that before it was broadcast on the SENSE agency, through the SENSE agency service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you say your source of that information is the news agency known as SENSE?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can have the -- I don't know if it's possible to get the audiotape brought back. She said -- well, she said differently. There's a part that's not in the transcript. I'm not here to testify on -- to act as translator, so I don't think I ought to translate the part that's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might ask her to repeat her answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There seems to be some dispute over what you actually said in your last answer. Could I ask you to repeat it, please. Do you want me to repeat my question to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know where his family got burnt down, whether in Prelovo or at some other place, before I saw on the SENSE service that he would be coming here to testify and to publicise those accusations here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So today you're not sure whether -- you're not sure that his family burnt to death in Prelovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information comes from the people. I don't know. I may not be qualified to judge where his family came to grieve, but I'd heard from other people that his house in Prelovo had been burned down and that his family had been burnt alive there. I know no more than that. I'm only telling you what I've heard. It's what people were saying, what people were telling each other, but I can say for sure that his family was burned alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In response to a question from Mr. Ivetic, you testified that Hamdija Vilic was a commander of a unit in the Bosnian Muslim army. That's at Transcript 3971 to 72. What rank did he hold as a commander? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I do know that he held a rank, but I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the name of his unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that lacks foundation, and it also assumes that all units have names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well ... do you know the name of his unit, Witness? Yes, I'm asking the question. Do you know the name of his unit, Witness? I'm asking you a question. Do you know the name of his unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, you need to turn off your mike before she answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. I just know that he was with the Bosnia army, but I don't know the name of his unit. I also know there were many different units in the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, just my last few questions to you. Your involvement in this case, did the Defence contact you, or did you contact the Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Defence contacted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've been put forward as a character witness, and you've given some very good character evidence or evidence of good character about Mr. Milan Lukic. You never came forward with that evidence to Mr. Sulacic, his prior attorney, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. If he's going to ask this, he's going to ask who for the Defence contacted her. He's skipping out a whole bunch of steps, and I think it's improper to ask a witness to take on an duty or obligation that they don't have. It's presenting a false picture to this Tribunal, and I've been sitting here listening to Mr. Groome, and thus far he's done better than with some other witnesses but I believe that this is the type of question that is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You haven't satisfied me that it is inappropriate, Mr. Ivetic, I regret to say. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you have some explanation as to why it took you 16 years to come forward with evidence of alibi that would exonerate Mr. Lukic for two very serious crimes and such important character evidence? Is there any explanation you have as to why it's taken so long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I took a long time to do that. As soon as I was contacted to appear as a witness, I responded. The way I see it, it didn't really take me that long. Even if it had been a hundred years, I would still have responded. I only had one father. That's what I said the last time around. I lost my mother too. I don't even remember her, and I can never forget a single good thing that anyone did to me, not even Milan Lukic's, and if this was about any other person and not Milan Lukic, my testimony, my evidence would still be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Over the course of the break, did you have any conversation with anyone about your testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I must put it to you plainly that it is my position that you've only come forward at this stage because you have been paid to provide this evidence that you've given in this case. Do you understand what I'm putting to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I think that she's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that she's answered this time and time again when Mr. Groome has asked her, and she's denied it each time, so what is the point of Mr. Groome putting this exact same question back to the witness multiple times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a practice in many jurisdictions to conclude by putting to the witness that the witness is fabricating, and I think it is perfectly proper to conclude a cross-examination in this way. What do you say to the question put to you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only state with full responsibility that everything Hamdija said about me was a fabrication.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) Please. What Hamdija said is totally pointless. The only point to his allegations is he can't stand me as a person, not just me, this applies to other members of my family, too because I live with a man who is a Catholic. If that bothers him so much, he might as well go and hang himself instead of coming up with all these fabrications against me. All of this is something that has been staged against me. Why and be whom exactly, I don't know. My apologies. Before he came when he saw me wearing shorts, because that's what I was wearing back home, he said that he would set fire to any woman who is not keeping warm. I have a right to live my life the way I see fit. I can live with a Catholic man, with a Serb, with whoever I like, but this is the most important thing that bothers everyone, including my family as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can -- at page 34, line 1, somewhere between there and line 2, although it doesn't appear in the transcript, the witness mentioned her name. Therefore, we need to have a redaction from the audio-video portion of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, is it your evidence that Hamdija Vilic is doing -- has done what he's done because he disapproves of your lifestyle and that you live with a Catholic man? Is that really your belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's my personal conviction, and I'm certain because there can't be any other reasons for him to act this way towards me. Maybe he should have found someone who would defend him in a different place and then, you know, pay 500.000 and not just this. And not, you know, like pin things such as these on my husband and me and slander our home. You know, this is simply unheard of. I've never heard of anything like this happening anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Has he ever said anything to you, Witness? Has he ever said anything to you to indicate that he disapproves of your living with a Catholic man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he did say that in public. He said he didn't agree with me living with a Catholic. He showed me this photograph on his mobile phone, his brother, the daughter. They were wearing veils - I'm not sure what I should call that - to cover their faces, and I know and I'm saying to you now, morally and materially, that he is an enormous nationalist, and this has nothing to do with this trial in itself. He and his brothers are nationalists, very fervent ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's interesting. And you think that his nationalism, his nationalistic fervor explains why he gave this testimony? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's the reason. That was the only reason that he came to my home and asked to see my family. This is all something that he staged and fabricated. He want to slander our house. He wanted to slander my family. I say this with full responsibility. If it is ever proven that I took any money at all, any money at all, a single Euro let alone more than that, I should be sent to prison. But I also ask that Hamdija's lies finally be put an end to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Finally, MLD10, during your evidence on the 18th of December, you unexpectedly testified to events of St. Vitus day, 1992, that we were told your brother MLD2 was scheduled to testify about. I have already put it to you that the real reason you no longer speak to your brother is that he is angry with you for not giving him all the money you received from Milan Lukic to secure his testimony. I now put to you the following: I put it to you that you unexpectedly volunteered MLD2's evidence during your testimony as a way of giving Milan Lukic what he has already paid for, an alibi for the 27th of June. Is that not the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this is the 10th, 15th time we've had it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Those are his instructions. I allowed you to put your case. He's putting his case. Those are his instructions. He's obliged to put it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, when we had Prosecution witnesses here, time and time again we were not allowed to ask things and repeat things. We were told to move along. We had very serious allegations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I never stopped you in cross-examination by concluding cross-examination by suggesting that a witness is fabricating, by putting your case, and this is what he's doing. Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state with full responsibility that I received no money at all. My relationship with my brother, my family, all this has nothing to do with Milan Lukic, his evidence. Why am I not speaking to my brother? Nothing to do with that. I don't get along with my brother because he spends time with people such as Hamdija. There was another neighbor. His name is Enes. He offended me. He called me an Ustasha slut. He went that far, and this is a quote. He took my brother's phone to call my home: Hello, gentlemen, I have a husband, I can't allow myself to talk to people like that, and my husband wouldn't let me go and see my brother and act like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, MLD10. I have no further questions. Your Honour, I would ask -- I've been working with the statement of MLD10. I'd like to tender it into evidence at this time. I'll get the Defence number in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement is admitted as P215, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, MLD10 for coming back to us to testify. I have just a few items to discuss with you relating to the cross-examination of Mr. Groome, and I bear your indulgence in answering those questions, and then I'll be finished with you, ma'am. First of all, the page that I have - and I'm told that my page numbers are different from the ones that are in the transcript - is page 4017. I'm told that ought to be 4017 of the transcript at lines 3 through 7 -- 3 through, actually, 11. Mr. Groome was asking you about how things changed in your home, that is to say with respect to certain intimidating phone calls that you were receiving, how things changed when you installed a cordless telephone respective to a prior telephone. Could you please tell us, what is the physical or technological difference between the telephone, the cordless telephone that you installed after which the phone calls abated and the prior telephone that you had had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the difference is like this. Now a number is shown. I know who the caller is, and there are no more disturbing calls. Sometimes it would happen that I got the heavy-breather calls, or people who would call me and just whistle across the line. It wasn't that I needed a cordless phone, but I wanted a number displayed. I wanted to know who the caller was. That's why I got one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the next series of questions, Your Honours, I'd ask to go into private session so as to protect the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I have no further questions for you. On behalf of the entire against team of Milan Lukic, I thank you most fervently for coming here to testify not once but twice, and we thank you for indulging us with your testimony and enduring those hard-ships to come here and testify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your testimony. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave. And we will adjourn. We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the outset of this afternoon's proceedings, I ought to have indicated that in the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to rule 15 bis. The witness is here. Let him make the declaration, unless Mr. Ivetic has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was advised that we probably ought to seek private session while the court is still considering this witness's application for protective matters. That's what that I would bring to Your Honours's attention as we are in open session at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have two short matters if I could raise them with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'd like to point out, Your Honour, that the Prosecution has not been provided with a written statement for this witness at the present time. We have only a brief summary, and you'll be aware, Your Honour, that this witness is a late-notified alibi witness. Mr. Ivetic has no doubt prepared his examination-in-chief carefully for this witness. I would now ask that Mr. Ivetic provide the Prosecution with a copy of all this witness's written statements at once and prior to his testifying. If it's the case that Mr. Ivetic is calling such an important witness without a written statement having been taken, I ask that Mr. Ivetic state for the record that no such written statement has been taken from the witness and that no such statement is in existence. That's the first matter. And secondly, Your Honour, I would ask that there be no leading questions of this witness, and in particular, no leading questions as to date, him being an alibi star witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the second matter I take for granted. Leading questions are not allowed except in relation to the very introductory matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Certainly not in relation to controversial issues. The Chamber counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, as to the first matter raised by Mr. Cole, Mr. Ivetic, again, I reiterate, if you have any written statements pertaining to this witness, then the rules oblige you to disclose them to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, I apologise, I don't know if Mr. Cole husband here when I made my comments earlier in the afternoon or not, this witness has never given a written statement to the Milan Lukic Defence team. I thus have no written statement to give for this viva voce witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's enough. Mr. Cole, as I indicated, to deal with the late notification in relation to this witness, we will hear the evidence-in-chief today, and at a later date we will notify the parties when cross-examination will take place. Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know how you wish to deal with the protective measures issues. You said you want the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Witness, please listen to me. Let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you know, my name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys for the accused Milan Lukic. I would -- first, I'll give the court reporter [sic] a chance to get back to her seat. The pseudonym sheet is there. I would first ask you to take a look at the pseudonym sheet, that with the assistance of the court officer, we be put in front of you, and without revealing your identity or that of any other persons contained therein, I would ask that you verify first your identity listed under the pseudonym of MLD15 and that the aforementioned contained therein is correct and accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to the individual that is listed as MLD16 on this sheet, I would ask that you also, while refraining from using that person's actual name when testifying and instead utilize the pseudonym listed. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with -- let me try and short-circuit some of these questions that I had anticipated doing in private session. I think if we avoid -- if we refrain from people's full names and deal with the pseudonyms, we can deal with some of these in open session. I apologize. If you could please sign that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And once that is done, Your Honours, I would ask that tender this pseudonym sheet into evidence as the next available 1D Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit 1D96 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And moving along, with regards to MLD16, the person that's identified as MLD16, can you tell us how it is that you know this person and how long you have known this person, again, without identifying the name or any biographical features that might identify this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: I know that girlfriend for a long time. I socialized with her. I practically grew up with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And first if I can ask you, if I could direct your attention to Mr. Milan Lukic, who is seated here behind me to my right, do you know this individual? First of all, is the question that I'm going to ask you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, Your Honours, before going into the specifics of how this individual knows Mr. Lukic, I'd ask to go into private session briefly to cover that. I've eliminated most of the other private session questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, did you have occasion to socialise with Milan Lukic in Belgrade at all, and if so, could you describe the extent of that social relationship.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: I had occasion to meet him in Belgrade several times. I was commuting between Switzerland and Belgrade. I still live in Switzerland. And at that time, we made an agreement to get together whenever possible. The nature of our relationship was great, super, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the occasions when you had socialized with Mr. Milan Lukic in Belgrade, was there any specific location or establishment which you would frequent when seeing one another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: At the time, we frequented restaurant Mata [phoen] next to the Zemun market-place. This was an in place for the young people to hang out in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could please explain for us what type of social interactions did you have with Milan Lukic? What kind of things did you talk about or participate in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: There were occasions when he would contact me, and since at that night I had been preparing a surprise party for my then-girlfriend, I had intention to present an engagement ring to her, I invited him to attend that party, and this was one of such occasions when we would meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the surprise party. We'll get to that in a second. What I was asking about was, in total, in general, what types of social interactions or activities did you engage in with Mr. Lukic in all of the times that you socialised with him while in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Our get-togethers would boil down to sports, small talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Entertainment, sports, girls.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, with respect to your socialising with Mr. Lukic, do you have any approximation as to how many times or how frequently you had socialised with him in Belgrade in this capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Well, not frequently but on several occasions, on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in the course of your social dealings with Mr. Milan Lukic, did you have occasion to get to know him enough to reach an opinion as to the type of person he was, and if so, what was your appraisal of him in this regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: He's a very cheerful person, ready to help another, always ready to have fun, likes to laugh and smile a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how would you describe Mr. Milan Lukic's interactions or relations with and treatment of persons of differing ethnic or religious backgrounds from his own during the time period that you knew and socialised with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: At that period, we had no reason to talk about ethnic affiliation, religious affiliation, about who was from where.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier that you had occasion of some sort of surprise party. If we can focus on that for a moment, could you tell us what surprise party you're talking about and when it occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: The surprise party for my then-girlfriend and future fiancée took place on the 7th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say the surprise party for your then-girlfriend and future fiancée, what was the purpose of that surprise party on the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: For the reason to make her like me even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... plans for that evening in relation to yourself and your then-girlfriend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In regard to your relationship between yourself and your then-girlfriend, what was the significance of that surprise party that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: It were to be a sit-down dinner, some drinks, and as a gathering of people we liked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have any special plans with regard to anything that you were going to do that evening with respect to your then-girlfriend, any significant event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Yes. I planned to give her an engagement ring, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, where was this surprise party to take place, what city, first of all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: At Zemun, part of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there a particular location in Zemun, that part of Belgrade, that this surprise party was to take place in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Then restaurant Mata or cafe, Mata, next door to the Zemun marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, I apologize. Just waiting for the translation and transcript. Was there a stated time for this surprise party to -- that it was supposed to take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: In the evening hours, between, let's say, 8 and 12 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and you indicated that you had some contact with Milan Lukic in regards to this. Could you explain the nature of the contact that you had with Milan Lukic in regards to this particular event that you've described, the surprise party at the restaurant Mata on the 7th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Yes. I was at home that day, and during that day I received a phone call from Milan to my home number, and he said that he was in Belgrade, and I took this opportunity to invite him to come to the party later in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, were there -- was he to be the only guest, or were there other guests that were -- that had been invited for that event, the surprise party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Yes. There were other guests invited. Among others, the MLD16.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall if in his contact with you Mr. Lukic advised the circumstances behind his being in Belgrade during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: It seemed to me that he had arrived to take his mother for a physical exam at a hospital with some other friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that other persons had been present for that event. I'd like to go into private session to see if we can identify some of those.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you could tell us, do you recall whether Mr. Lukic arrived for this party early -- or what time did he arrive for this party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: The party had already begun, and then MLD was already there. I remember this because when Milan walked in, she had apparently had a quarrel with him at some point previously, so she stood up and left, and then I drove her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can dilate on that a little bit, focus on that. When you say she stood up and left, was that an expected reaction? How did you react to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: It was really surprising. I hadn't seen it coming myself. That much is certain. That's why the encounter sticks in my memory, and I ended up driving her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say you ended up driving her home. First of all, when did you drive her home? That is to say, did you remain with your then-girlfriend at the party, or did you leave with MLD16?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, at line 22 of this page, I believe we have the name of his then-girlfriend, to be fiancée. If we can have that redacted for -- in line with the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you have occasion to speak with MLD16, and what was your reaction to what had transpired while driving MLD16 home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: My reaction was that of surprise, but it's not like I had time to react because she was the one who kept talking to me all the time. She has an energetic character.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How would you describe your -- strike that. Did the reactions of MLD16 to Mr. Lukic's arrival at your surprise party, did they have an effect on your relationship or your disposition towards MLD16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: No. There was no negativity involved. Quite the contrary, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to -- strike that. When you took MLD16 home, you said you came back to the party, when is the next time that you saw Mr. Milan Lukic after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "... two days later there was a different cafe," what do you mean? What transpired two days later at a different cafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: We were in the poolroom at Miet [phoen] in Saradusana [phoen] Street, and we played pool there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "we," to which individuals are you referring to? Who is the "we" in your response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Milan and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say Milan -- could you please give his full name so we have -- so there's no confusion, the full name of the Milan with whom you were playing billiards at the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while you're playing billiards with Milan Lukic two days after the 7th of June, 1992, first of all, where is that Saradusana Street located, what city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Zemun. This restaurant or poolroom is right next to my former flat, a flat in which I had been born and grown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to playing the billiards with Milan Lukic that day, what, if anything, transpired apart from the billiards?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 64, line 11, again, Your Honours, if we can have the first name of his late wife redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I could just assist in terms of your testimony. When referring to your late wife, if we could refer to her without her name. That way we can avoid having your identity perhaps revealed to persons who might be able to garner from her name your identity. Now, with respect -- sorry. And with respect to your conversation with your then-girlfriend, fiancee, what transpired in the course of that telephonic conversation wherein she stated that MLD16 was present at your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: Following that conversation, I know that she and Milan and she made it up. I told her where I was and who I was with, so she came over. I know that they made it up that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to -- with respect to Milan Lukic, did you have occasion to meet with him at any point in time after that occasion on the 9th of June -- did you have any other time after that occasion in the billiard hall in Zemun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD15
utterances.text: No, not after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Those are all the questions that I have prepared for you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm finished with the direct, and unless Your Honours have questions, I presume we'll be moving on to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's quite so because as I indicated, the Chamber has decided to defer the cross-examination of this witness for the reasons already stated. Witness, you are going to be excused from court now, and you'll be told when to return. You may leave. Before you leave, I should tell you that you are not to discuss your evidence with anybody. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The next witness, Your Honours, is MLD3 who had previously been granted protective measures pursuant to the -- one moment. Who had been previously granted protective measures by Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness, may I inquire whether the statement -- oh, I'm sorry. We have the statement for this. I withdraw it. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I have been told that the witness has declined protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was going to be my first question. He had mentioned this this morning to me in proofing that he wished to testify in open court, and I was going ask him if he still stood by that decision and then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you wish to testify in open court, publicly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As far as there is one other individual that has been previously granted protective measures that this testimony might touch, I would still proceed with the pseudonym sheet with regards to identifying that particular person. Yeah. Let's wait for that. I guess, Your Honours, to make efficient use of the time, I would ask the witness to identify himself for the record by stating his full name while we wait for the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goran Djeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Djeric, where do you currently reside, in what city?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Obrenovac, Zabrizido Stevo [phoen], number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask the court usher's assistance in showing you the pseudonym sheet for purposes of directing your attention to the last half of the pseudonym sheet where you see an individual that is identified there as MLD4.
