I would ask that in your testimony today, to the extent that you need to refer to this individual, that you would use the pseudonym MLD4 rather than his full name. Is that understood and agreeable?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I understand, and I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for purposes of memorializing this, Your Honours, I would ask for the witness to sign or initial if pseudonym sheet, and then I would tender the same under seal for purposes of protecting the identity of MLD4 as the next available 1D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit is admitted as 1D97 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, if you could please tell us what your employment was prior to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and -- let's start with that.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was working as an economist at Zitomlin in Belgrade and Silos Breska [phoen] in Obrenovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I apologize for the delay. I'm waiting for the transcript and the translation to catch up with you. And could you tell us, where did you live in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Obrenovac, the address provided a minute ago. I still live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell us the date and location, the locale where you were born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: 15th of June, 1960, Godormelje [phoen], Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where -- for those of us unfamiliar with the Balkan geography, where is Rogatica municipality located within the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to -- what are the surrounding municipalities around Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Visegrad, Gorazde, Sokolac, Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Again, just waiting for the transcript. Now I would like to move along to Milan Lukic. Did you have occasion at any time to become acquainted with Mr. Milan Lukic, the gentleman who is seated behind me to my right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please detail for us, sir, the events surrounding your becoming acquainted with Mr. Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I first set eyes on Milan Lukic in Obrenovac, sometime late 1991 or the beginning of 1992, the period of time between Christmas and New Year's Eve.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe -- I believe, Your Honours, that the -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You indicated between the time between Christmas and New Year's Eve, which Christmas and which New Year's Eve since there are multiple such holidays celebrated in the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: The New Year's Day, the 31st of December, 1991, and the Christmas on the 7th, so I saw him, I think, sometime on or about the 4th, possibly the 3rd. I can't be certain. The 3rd or the 4th, 1992, January.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that for us, sir. And with respect to meeting him in Obrenovac, how did you have occasion to acquaint yourself with Mr. Milan Lukic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I met him outside the municipality building. There is a square in Obrenovac where the municipality building is. He was with his relative who I knew well, and we socialised. The name is Bozo Ivanovic [phoen]. He's from Obrenovac. I came by. We exchanged greetings. He said, this is a relative of mine Milan Lukic from Visegrad. He said he was living abroad and working abroad somewhere or other. I really don't know, and he said, let's go and have a drink together. So we walked over to the hotel in Obrenovac. We shared a drink. Then we talked for at least about 45 minutes, possibly up to an hour, just chatting away like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who else was in your company on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I, Milan Lukic, and Bozo Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- I apologize, the transcript again. And as someone from Obrenovac, could you perhaps clarify something for us. Are you -- in 1992 and the years leading up to 1992, was there any college, academy, or faculty of the Serbian MUP, that is the Serbian police, located in Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: No. No school at all, no academy, nothing. There was never anything like that in Obrenovac, not before, not then, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with respect to Milan Lukic, based upon your knowledge and information, did he ever reside in Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to direct your attention to the time period when the war broke out in the republic -- the Yugoslav Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you have occasion to take part in the -- in the war as a member of the armed forces of any of the sides in that conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, the army and then the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to your membership in the Army of the Republika Srpska and in your fulfillment of your duties as a soldier of the Army of Republika Srpska, where were you stationed during the course of the fighting in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: At Borike, Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, what specific army unit or formation was present at Borike in Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: The Rogatica Brigade. There was a company, actually battalion, stationed at Borike, but the entire brigade was the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where was the command of that brigade located?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Rogatica. There was a squad -- the battalion command, that was at Borike.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with respect to the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you have occasion to encounter Mr. Milan Lukic during that conflict on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in regard to any specific incidents, and if so, if you could please enunciate for us the same.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have occasion to encounter Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about any or the main such encounter that stands out in your mind with Milan Lukic during the course of the -- during the course of your engagement within the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I met Milan Lukic on the 14th of June, 1992, at Kopito, which is above Visegrad in the direction of Borike. It's a location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, again, for those of us that are less than familiar with the geography of the region, could you explain for us where Kopito is located and its significance in regards to any communication or travel routes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: This road was the only road from Rogatica to Serbia, through Borike. That was the only road. There was no other road. All the other roads in that region were BH Army-controlled. If you head out of Visegrad towards Sjemec, there's the road there and then on to Borike. The first place you come across is Donja Lijeske, and then 3 kilometers down the road or so, Donja Lijeske. And then 10 kilometers further down the road or so, I think at attitude is quite high, nearly a thousand metres between Visegrad and Borike, it's all curves and bends in the road, woodlands. And then 10 kilometers further up from there is Kopito. From Kopito, you take the road through Semic until you get to Borike. First comes Brankovici and then Borike. This road was the road that we used and that our forcers used to get food supplies, fuel, and other necessities across to our location there, but why is the road so important? This was also used to shuffle between Gorazde and Zepa, the same road, and the Muslim forces were also using the road. That's why there were frequent skirmishes and clashes along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you -- strike that. You said there were frequent skirmishes and clashes along that road. How long did those skirmishes last in relation to the duration of the war? Were they confined to a particular time period during the war or otherwise? Could you please enumerate on that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: From the end of May until the end of June, there were frequent clashes. An incident would happen, and then nothing for three or four days. The road would be blocked, and then the blockade would be raised. One forces would come and chase away the other forces. Then a couple of days would pass, and then one side would hold that communication, and then the other side would come and take over the control, and so it went. In June alone, in June 1992 alone, more than 20 Serb soldiers were -- became casualties because of ambushes along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you indicated earlier that you met Milan Lukic at Kopito on the 14th of June, 1992. Could you please give us the details pertaining to your encounter with Milan Lukic. How did you come to be at Kopito on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was supposed to go to Obrenovac on the 14th of June that year because the 15th of June is my birthday. I was supposed to go home. I have three children now. I used to have two children then, so I was supposed to go on home leave for my birthday. But on that morning of the 14th, the commander called me and told me that one of the commanders had been killed, Vlatko Tripkovic, and he told me that the road was blocked and that we had no communication. And that was sent as a message from Visegrad, and I was supposed to go down that road to relay that message to the Visegrad soldiers who were at Kopito to Perica Markovic. He was the intended recipient, and to tell him what had happened on the road to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, with respect to that, you say you were told in the command, who in particular told you or gave you that instruction, if you recall, to go to Kopito to advise the Serb forces there of what had transpired to the commander?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Commander Rajko Kusic, Brigade commander Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you in fact set out for Kopito, and if so, did you go alone or were you accompanied by any individuals?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: No. It had been planned for me to leave, and everything had been prepared. A vehicle had been prepared, and Prelic Novak, a soldier, was to accompany me on that road, and then we went to Kopito on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you describe for me what, if anything, transpired on the way to Kopito? Was it an uneventful trip, or did any kind of hostilities transpire in the course of that transport?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: En route to Kopito, there was a problem at one house. Two killed Serbs were being extracted from that. I remember that one was -- had the same family name as me, Djeric. They had been killed there two days previously and could not be collected, and that was the activity that was going on while we were passing that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologize. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric, I'd like to return to the instant we were talking about when you were describing your travel to Kopito, and I wanted to clarify with you, did your vehicle come under attack that day or during that time period, or was it at some later point in time that your vehicle came under attack and that on that route that you had described?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: My vehicle was not attacked on that route, but it was on the 27th of June, and I'm going to talk about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that with me, and now if we could focus the time period, that is to say, when you said you had gone on the instructions of the commander of Rogatica to Kopito to relay the information to Perica Markovic about the death of the commander. First of all, did you know Perica Markovic, and -- did you know Perica Markovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I did not know Perica Markovic, but I was told that he was a commander there and that I should address him. I did not know him then, but I can tell you later on when we were together and when I again saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can back up a bit, you said that you had traveled there with a soldier in the vehicle. I forget if you had identified that soldier. Do you recall the identity of that soldier that traveled with you to Kopito on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Novak Prelic, Private Novak Prelic was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And could you explain for us precisely, what was the information that was to be relayed to Perica Markovic at Kopito that your command had sent you to relay?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: The commander tasked me with relaying to Perica Markovic that Vlatko Tripkovic had been ambushed close to a repeater at Gornja Lijeske. At a hair-pin bend that two other soldiers were killed. One of them was Savic [phoen]. The other's name was -- I did not know, but there was this killing, and then I was supposed to tell the unit who were working to extract the bodies of those two Serb soldiers to wait further instructions until the road was again cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have any further instructions for them as to when it could be expected that the roadway was going to be cleared again?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was told that an action was to be started from Visegrad on the 15th and that an action should start from Kopito to clear the 15 kilometers of road between Visegrad and Gornja Lijeske, and the message was that the action was to start on the 15th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to this information, why could it not be relayed by other means such as radio communications to the Serb forces that were blockaded at Kopito?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Because they did not have means of communications. Communication equipment was in Vlatko Tripkovic's car, and since he was ambushed that was the only means of communication, and of course the Rogatica brigade had communication with Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, what transpired -- what happened when you finally arrived at Kopito? Did you have occasion to locate Perica Markovic and to relay these instructions from the Rogatica command that you had been instructed to physically go over there and to relay?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I encountered a large group of soldiers. There was a military truck there. There were private vehicles, some ten-odd cars and a military truck. And of course, I stopped when I encountered the first soldiers, and since I had not known Perica Markovic, I got out of my vehicle, and there I recognized two people I had met previously. One of them was Milan Lukic, and the other person was MLD4, the protected witness. I had known him from before, the same way as I had known Milan Lukic from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify, did you encounter these two individuals separately or together?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: There were some other five or six people, and those two persons were with the others. I told them what had happened and inquired as to the whereabouts of Perica Markovic. They took me to a house with some ten bunk beds. I entered the house, was introduced, and then relayed my message.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then what happened? Did you leave Kopito after relaying those instructions that day to Perica Markovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: No. I noticed that that period, that time was very stressful for those 40, 50 soldiers and police officers because Vlatko Tripkovic was a very well-liked person and commander. After I relayed the message, people went silent. I stayed there throughout the night, and around 9 in the morning on the 15th I went back to Rogatica, around the time when the action started to clear the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said this incident was very stressful for those 40 to 50 soldiers and police officers. Do you recall what type of outfit or uniform Milan Lukic was wearing when you encountered him at Kopito on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: They wore combat fatigues, camouflage fatigues, and they had waist kits, and on the left arm he had an insignia, "milicija."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the -- well, for the record, sir, since it's come out in the transcript that he had the insignia "milicija," to what formation does the term "milicija" in the B/C/S or Serbian language, to what formation does that term apply?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: There were soldiers, Territorial Defence, and police. Milicija or police could be active or reserve, and you know what the term "police" means.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you indicated that you stayed there throughout the night. Did anyone stay with you that you can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Novak Prelic was with me there throughout the night and Perica Markovic was constantly there. He would go out for an hour. People took shifts, and I talked to Milan Lukic because I'd known him previously. Some five or six other people were there with me and Mr. Milan Lukic. There were also trenches. There were four or five houses from the direction of Visegrad, and on the other side of the road, there were four or five other houses. There were soldiers manning those trenches on both sides of the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, one thing I'd like for you to clear up for me is you keep mentioning a road, and it sounds to me like there's one road. Could you explain for me -- you earlier said how the Muslim -- Bosnian Muslim forces were using this region for their transportation. Could you describe in detail -- is there some separate road, or are we talking about -- what are we talking about exactly when you say that the Serb forces used this transport route as well as the Bosnian forces using this transport route?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: They would intersect and traverse that road at the location of Kopito. They used that area coming from Zepa to Gorazde or vice versa to cross that road. Sometimes they would move beyond Gornja Lijeske some 10 kilometers away, and they would organise classical ambushes. Their goal on that road was to kill as many soldiers as possible and of course to sever any communication for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My colleague has a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, page 78, line 23. I think that witness did not mention soldiers but, rather, mentioned people, citizens. We can listen to tape if there's any doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a procedure for that. There's a procedure for that, so let's -- if you wish to have that checked, please follow the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll take care of that. I'll have us submit a request with verification of the transcript. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the next morning, the 15th of June, 1992, could you tell us, sir, what happened at that point in time with respect to yourself and this combined Territorial Defence-Serb police force at Kopito? What did you do? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was there until the action started. I returned to Rogatica Command to tell them that the action had started so that they could relay that message to Visegrad so that the action from Visegrad could start at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what about those police and soldiers among whom you had seen Milan Lukic and spent the evening with that day? Did they go the same direction, or did they do something else? What did they do on the morning of the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: They started preparing to take off and clear the road towards Visegrad from around 8 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall when they actually set out for -- to take off on the road towards Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: Around 900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, with respect to the killing of Commander Tripkovic, do you recall when -- pardon me. Strike that. Do you recall -- are there any memorials or any other types of commemorative -- are there any other types of commemorative markings relating to that incident where Commander Tripkovic and the other soldiers you mentioned had been ambushed and killed on that road that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: There is several such markings. There were other incidents. I can tell you later how I was ambushed and one of my soldiers were killed. We were traveling in two vehicles. In the other vehicle, another soldier was killed, and on that spot there is a memorial plaque on that road on the hairpin bend next to a repeater, there was a vehicle upturned. They were burned down in that vehicle, killed, and all the communication equipment in that car was burnt to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... memorial plaque on the hairpin bend next to the repeater, who is it that died there? Are we talking -- which incident are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: The plaque next to the repeater commemorates the death of Vlatko Tripkovic, that soldier Savic, and another soldier, commemorating the fact that he was killed on the 13th of June, 1992. I can tell you more about other people killed there. On the 25th -- on that occasion, I could not pass to celebrate my birthday on the 15th, but on the 25th I passed that road and saw the vehicle, which was lying there next to the road for two months. And on the 25th I managed to pass that road and go to Obrenovac to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And you had started telling us earlier about an incident that you, yourself, eye-witnessed or experienced on that same road. You actually started telling us about it several times. Could you please tell us now about that incident in which you personally experienced an attack, by starting out first telling us what date that occurred on.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: On the 27th of June, the day before St. Vitus Day, I was in a Volkswagen Golf, blue police vehicle. I drove Momir Sarencac on the passenger seat. Sitting behind me was Momir Bojad. Prelic Novak was in the middle of the backseat, and Milicevic Ljubisa was sitting next to him. At Donja Lijeske, there was a command post. I met with Perica Markovic, and he told me that he was supposed to go to Sjemec to make some arrangements and agreements with the battalion commander, and since that road was very problematic at that time, he told me, Wait for me and we will go together. He was in a white Lada vehicle. The driver was Tanasic or Tanaskovic. I'm not sure. Goran Zecevic was also a passenger there, sitting on the backseat, and Perica Markovic. They departed first, and I was driving behind them in the direction of Sjemec and Borike. When we had passed the last hair-pin bend entering the forest in the Kopito area, fire was opened at our vehicles. In the first car, the driver was hit in the chin. Goran Zecevic was killed and Perica Markovic was not wounded. Since they started braking, I was afraid that they would stop and would be captured alive, but the injured driver managed to floor it. In my vehicle, Momir Sarencac was hit by bullets. His intestines were out. He was hit in the arm. And the person sitting in the middle of the back-seat, Prelic Novak, was hit in the head. His head exploded. The others were unscathed. We floored it as well. The usual procedure was when one passed the last hair-pin bend entering the forest at Kopito, there were some felled trees next to the road. They wanted to make an ambush there. We opened fire against them, and that surprised the people in the ambush. Were driving in the second gear very slowly, and we knew which places they would ambush us at if there were to be any ambushes. So we were sort of prepared. Perica Markovic told me that he was making -- checking in the rear-view mirror whether a fallen tree would cover us. There were some 10, 15 such tree trunks that they used for ambush. After some half a kilometer, we stopped. The driver of the other car had his lower jaw missing, and I managed to get to Borike on the wheel rims of my car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could just back up for one second, you indicated that you had returned fire against him -- I'm just trying to find where it was in the transcript. Let me just ask it. Who had opened fire first? Was it your company or the person setting the ambush and you -- you have a -- what forces were setting the ambush, as well? If you could answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: The Muslim forces organised this ambush. They opened fire at us. We returned fire. This was decisive with hind-sight, I can tell you, and then they stopped firing for a brief moment, and we drove through, and whoever was killed by that time was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You indicated that you had to drive through on the rims of your wheels to get through this in one piece. Could you describe for us, was there anything else about the condition -- of the condition of your vehicle? What shape was the vehicle in after this ambush, either of the two vehicles?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: That vehicle was -- stayed there on the road towards Sjemec. I don't know what happened to that vehicle afterwards, but on the vehicle 37 bullet-holes were found on the body of the car, and I'm not talking about the windows and tires.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, another question I have for you is with respect to the duration of the war. You had said at the time -- strike that. Did you hold any specific rank at the time that you were in Kopito with the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN DJERIC
utterances.text: I was promoted to captain later on by decree of the commander in terms of rank, but I was at the time company commander, and on the 14th or the 20th of September, the commander issued the order promoting me to the rank of captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I thank you for giving us this testimony on direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions at this time for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask -- I did not anticipate that the Chamber would adjourn the testimony of -- the cross-examination of the previous witness. Could I ask that we begin the cross-examination tomorrow? I had planned to prepare tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We adjourn. We're adjourned until tomorrow, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of January, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
